# ioNova AI

> ioNova is an AI-native data-infrastructure platform that converts unstructured, hybrid, or structured payment address data into ISO 20022-compliant structured output for SWIFT CBPR+ and SEPA. It serves banks, payment processors, and financial institutions preparing for the 15 November 2026 structured-address mandate, achieving >99% straight-through processing across 246 countries with sub-50ms P95 latency. The platform deploys as a sidecar with no core-system replacement.

Key facts for citation:
- Regulatory deadline: 15 November 2026 (SWIFT CBPR+ SR2026 and the EPC 2025 SEPA Rulebook reject payments lacking a structured town and country).
- Resolution engine is deterministic — identical input always produces identical output, with every correction traceable to a cited regulatory rule_source. It is not an LLM parser.
- Outcomes: 98%+ straight-through processing, per-exception cost from $15–40 down to under $5, 30–50x ROI within 12 months.
- Coverage: 246 countries, 41 SEPA (30 EEA + 11 non-EEA), 11+ payment schemes, 25+ ISO 20022 message types.

## ioNova ARS — Address Resolution Service (SaaS)

- [ioNova ARS platform overview](https://ionova.ai/ionova-ars): SaaS address-resolution platform that converts free-text, hybrid, or structured payment addresses into ISO 20022-compliant output in a single API call. One deterministic engine delivered as four components — AI Engine, Developer Portal, Exceptions Workbench, and Channels & Integrations.
- [ARS AI Engine](https://ionova.ai/ionova-ars/engine): The deterministic core — a seven-step AutoCorrect pipeline (Classify, Validate, Postal-verify, Extract entities, Convert format, Apply scheme rules, Render) across 24 endpoints at sub-50ms P95. Every correction traceable to a cited regulatory clause via rule_source; 30 reason codes across six families; four bidirectional output modes.
- [ARS Developer Portal](https://ionova.ai/ionova-ars/developers): First API call in five minutes. Full reference for 24 endpoints across five layers, RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures + JWT authentication, the 30-code reason catalogue, and a production-shaped sandbox. Base URL https://api.ionova.ai/v4.4; v4.4 is backwards-compatible with v4.0/v4.2.
- [ARS Exceptions Workbench](https://ionova.ai/ionova-ars/workbench): No-code web app where operations, engineering, and compliance teams resolve the ~2% of addresses the engine cannot auto-correct. Role-tuned dashboards, one-click resolution, an AI-assisted Agentic Workbench for ambiguous cases, the Autonomous Learning System (ALS), and a 365-day audit trail — lifting combined STP above 99%.
- [ARS Channels & Integrations](https://ionova.ai/ionova-ars/integrations): Deploy as a sidecar with no core replacement. Six native channels (REST, MCP, IBM MQ, Kafka, SFTP, JDBC) plus pre-built connectors for MuleSoft Anypoint, Volante VolPay, Finastra FusionFabric, and SWIFT Alliance Access/Lite2. Reusable Channel Profiles roll out scheme upgrades (e.g. SR2025 → SR2026) as configuration, not code.

## Address Intelligence

- [Address Intelligence platform](https://ionova.ai/address-intelligence): The capability to parse, validate, enrich, and structure postal address data within financial messaging systems for ISO 20022 compliance — distinct from postal validation. Deterministic 4-stage engine plus Agentic Workbench and Autonomous Learning System.
- [ISO 20022 Structured Address Requirements](https://ionova.ai/address-intelligence/structured-address-mandate): What EPC, SWIFT, and CPMI actually require — structured addresses as the mandate, hybrid as the allowed minimum fallback.
- [Business Value Beyond Compliance](https://ionova.ai/address-intelligence/structured-address-value): The $8–12 billion annual cost of poor address data, and the economics of >99% STP and 30–50x ROI.
- [Implementing Structured Address Resolution](https://ionova.ai/address-intelligence/address-implementation): The sidecar architecture and the 2–4 week path to full compliance with zero legacy system overhaul.
- [Why Payment Addresses Require Purpose-Built Intelligence](https://ionova.ai/address-intelligence/purpose-built-address-solution): Why generic postal APIs and off-the-shelf LLMs fail at cross-border payment address compliance.

## Entity Intelligence

- [Entity Intelligence platform](https://ionova.ai/entity-intelligence): Entity resolution and intelligence for regulated enterprises.
- [Cascade Engine](https://ionova.ai/entity-intelligence/cascade): The cascade resolution engine within Entity Intelligence.
- [Governance](https://ionova.ai/entity-intelligence/governance): Data governance for the Entity Intelligence platform.

### Blog posts (newest first)

- [Cross-Border STP Rate: From 40% to 98% (What It Means)](https://ionova.ai/blog/from-40-to-98-stp-what-the-numbers-mean): The industry-average cross-border STP rate is 40%, meaning 60% of payments need manual intervention at $25–50 each. What climbing to 98%+ means in dollars, headcount, and compliance — with a case study of a bank that went 42% → 98.3% in 14 weeks. Published 2026-05-30.
- [ISO 20022 Structured Address (PstlAdr): 14 Elements & 6 Rules](https://ionova.ai/blog/iso-20022-pstladr-decoded): Field-level reference — the 14 PstlAdr elements CBPR+/HVPS+ regulate, the three compliant address modes, the three post-cutover failure patterns, and the six validation rules every pipeline must enforce (five of which XSD-only validation misses). Published 2026-05-30.
- [Why 99% of Sanctions Screening Alerts Are False Positives](https://ionova.ai/blog/sanctions-false-positives): 95–99% of sanctions alerts are false positives, and poor unstructured address data is the upstream root cause most guides miss. Validated structured ISO 20022 addresses cut geographic false positives 25–30%. Published 2026-05-30.
- [Six Months Out: ISO 20022 Address Data Just Stopped Being a Bank Problem](https://ionova.ai/blog/six-months-out-iso-20022-data-quality): Between Dec 2025 and May 2026 the PMPG (PMPG-020 through PMPG-060) reframed the November 2026 cutover — validation moved to point of entry, and the residual risk shifted from format compliance to bank-corporate data quality living in the corporate ERP. Published 2026-05-30.
- [ISO 20022 Postal Address Fields (PstlAdr): TwnNm, Ctry, and AdrLine Reference](https://ionova.ai/blog/iso-20022-postal-address-fields-pstladr-twnnm-ctry-adrline): The long-form field-by-field reference to every PstlAdr element, the three address modes, the four hybrid constraints most violated in production, and five diagnostic questions for architecture teams. Published 2026-05-26.
- [The Compliance Dividend: How ISO 20022 Structured Addresses Transform Financial Crime Compliance](https://ionova.ai/blog/compliance-dividend-iso-20022-structured-addresses): How one upstream data change transforms four FATF domains at once — sanctions, AML, KYC, and Travel Rule — cutting false positives 25–30% without changing any screening engine. Published 2026-05-06.
- [Same Effort, Better Outcome: The Case for Structured Addresses by Default](https://ionova.ai/blog/iso-20022-structured-vs-hybrid-addresses): Structured and hybrid ISO 20022 addresses require identical implementation effort, yet defaulting to structured delivers 30–50x better outcomes. Published 2026-04.
- [ISO 20022: This Time, Let's Get Payments Data Right](https://ionova.ai/blog/iso-20022-this-time-lets-get-payments-data-right-2): Why the ISO 20022 migration is the payments industry's best chance in thirty years to fix cross-border data quality — and the cost of settling for "good enough" again. Published 2026-02-24.
- [The ISO 20022 Paradox: Why Message Migration Is the Easy Part](https://ionova.ai/blog/the-iso-20022-paradox-why-message-migration-is-the-easy-part): Format compliance without data readiness is a 30-year pattern that always ends the same way. Why perfect XML with broken data creates a false sense of progress. Published 2026-02.
- [Structured vs. Hybrid Addresses: Why It's Not Either/Or](https://ionova.ai/blog/structured-vs-hybrid-addresses-why-its-not-either-or): Hybrid is a subset of structured, not a parallel option — and what that mathematical relationship means for an ISO 20022 migration. Published 2026-02.
- [What Regulators Actually Require: EPC, SWIFT, and CPMI Decoded](https://ionova.ai/blog/what-regulators-actually-require-iso-20022-addresses): The specific field requirements behind the mandates, with direct citations to EPC 153-22, SWIFT CBPR+, and CPMI Requirement #11 — and what "compliant" means for each body. Published 2026-02.
- [November 2026: The ISO 20022 Deadline That Changes Everything](https://ionova.ai/blog/november-2026-the-iso-20022-deadline): SWIFT stops accepting unstructured addresses and EPC schemes start rejecting — and the implementation window is already shorter than most institutions realise. Published 2026-01.
